muse_spark_1.3/001: The strategy is hunt-target with full probability density. All ship placements for lengths 5,4,3,3,2 that do not cover a miss are enumerated. In hunt mode the next shot maximizes the number of remaining placements covering it, which is the greedy maximum P(hit) and naturally favors the center. In target mode connected hit components are found, isolated components with no unknown neighbour are considered sunk, focus is put on the largest active component and its unknown orthogonal frontier is scored by placements that cover both the candidate and an adjacent hit, with a large bonus for covering multiple hits to force line extensions. Tie breaks use hunt heat, checker parity and centrality. A safe fallback scan guarantees a legal move.
muse_spark_1.3/002: The strategy is hunt-target with sunk-inference and probability heatmaps. All hits are grouped into orthogonal components. Linear components blocked at both ends are declared sunk and removed from the remaining fleet `[5,4,3,3,2]`. Remaining placements that avoid misses and sunk cells are enumerated to build a heatmap; when unsunk hits exist only placements touching them are counted. Targeting priority is: gaps between aligned unsunk hits, extensions of linear multi-hit groups, adjacent cells of single hits, picked by maximal heat. Otherwise the maximal heat unknown cell is chosen for hunting, giving center-biased efficient search with checkerboard tie-break. A guaranteed legal fallback is always provided.
muse_spark_1.3/003: The strategy is probability hunting combined with focused targeting. When no hits are known the bot counts, for every remaining ship length, all placements that avoid misses and scores each cell by how many placements cover it, firing at the maximum which naturally favours the centre and parity. When hits exist hits are grouped into orthogonal clusters. Linear clusters generate end-extension candidates, singletons generate 4-neighbour candidates, non-linear touching-ship clusters generate all neighbours. All placements that contain a whole cluster while avoiding misses vote for their unknown cells to form a target heatmap. Candidates are then chosen by maximum target heat with hunt heat as tie-break, guaranteeing continuation of the most constrained ship and automatic gap-filling between split hits, with full fallback to hunt and to first unknown to always stay legal.
muse_spark_1.3/004: The strategy is hunt-target with probability density and sunk filtering. All hits are grouped into 4-connected components. A linear component with both ends blocked by misses or edges is classified as sunk and ignored, all other components are active. Remaining ship lengths are the full fleet minus sunk lengths. Every legal placement of every remaining ship that avoids misses and sunk cells is enumerated; in hunt mode all placements vote, in target mode only placements covering an active hit vote. Votes accumulate into a heatmap on unknown cells. In hunt mode the max heat cell is chosen with chessboard parity and centre bias as tie-breaks to guarantee finding length-2 ships quickly. In target mode only orthogonal frontier cells are considered, and for multi-hit components only the axis ends are considered to avoid wasting side shots, picking the frontier cell with highest target heat. This finishes ships in minimal moves while the adaptive heatmap focuses search where long ships can still fit. A safe fallback guarantees a legal move.
muse_spark_1.3/005: Strategy is hunt-target with probability density. Hits are grouped into orthogonal components; a component with no adjacent unknown is considered sunk/closed and treated as blocked, others are active. Remaining fleet is estimated by removing closed straight components matching lengths 5,4,3,3,2. A placement is valid if it avoids misses and closed hits. In hunt mode with no active hits, score each unknown by how many valid placements cover it and pick the max, tie-broken by checkerboard parity and centre preference. In target mode candidate moves are restricted to unknown neighbours of active hits, scored by how many valid placements that touch any active hit cover them, which naturally prioritises line extensions for multi-hit ships and all neighbours for single hits, with hunt score as tie-break. All logic is O(10x10 placements) and wrapped in a failsafe that always returns an unfired cell.
